messages.author: f6d77eeabf5acd39
messages.subject: Priors on variance parameters
parts:
Hi all! 

I have 3 questions:

1. Is it possible to adapt the hyperparameters of prior distributions on the variance parameters in blavaan, and are there some 'rules' of guidelines when it is possible to change these values?

2. Is it possible to adapt the prior distributions on variance parameters? For example: Use the default Mplus prior on latent factor variances IW(0, -3) instead of the blavaan default W(I, 3). Or the mplus default IG(-1, 0) instead of the blavaan default G(1, 0.5) for residual variances?



If (2) is possible, then I have another question regarding the translation from an inverse gamma to a gamma distribution:

3. I found here that the default priors in blavaan are placed on precisions instead of variances, while Mplus placed prior distributions on the variances. I also found that a gamma prior on the precision equals an inverse gamma distribution on the variance. 

Does this mean that the Mplus default prior on the variance IG(-1,0) equals G(-1,0) on the precision in blavaan?
And the blavaan default prior on the precision G(1, 0.5) equal IG(1, 0.5) on the variance?


Any guidance or advice would be appreciated! Thanks!

Sanne Smid

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Priors on variance parameters
parts:
Sanne,

You can indeed change the prior distributions on precisions/variances however you wish. This page gives further info:

http://faculty.missouri.edu/~merklee/blavaan/prior.html

Notice that you can say something like "dunif(0,100)[sd]" to put the prior on the standard deviation instead of the precision (and there is also a "[var]" modifier for variance).

Regarding when to change the prior on the variance/precision, I do not have a definite answer here. I have noticed that the defaults in blavaan might be too informative for small sample sizes, so a sensitivity analysis could be especially useful in that case.

You are correct that inverse gamma on variance is the same as gamma on precision. But it is impossible to match the Mplus defaults in blavaan, because blavaan requires a proper prior distribution (and a gamma or IW distribution with a negative number is improper). This constraint cannot be overcome because JAGS (the underlying MCMC software) requires proper priors. But, aside from matching Mplus defaults, I don't think this constraint is very problematic or limiting.

Ed
